questions.question: Give a detailed account on the contributions of Sigmund Frued.
questions.solution_html:
• Give a detailed account on the contributions of Sigmund Frued.
  • Answer: Psychoanalysis, the structure of personality (Id, Ego, Superego), the concept of the
  • unconscious, and the psychosexual stages of development. Freud was the founder of the
  • psychodynamic perspective, which posits that many aspects of behavior stem from hidden
  • forces within our personalities and unconscious mind. His key contributions
  • include:Structure of Personality: He divided personality into three parts: the id (the primitive part
  • focused on pleasure), the ego (the rational part that deals with reality), and the superego (the moral center
  • or conscience)Psychosexual Stages: Freud theorized that personality develops through five stages of
  • physical and emotional growth, known as psychosexual stages.Level of Consciousness-The
  • Unconscious: He believed that the unconscious mind stores repressed conflicts and desires that can
  • manifest in outward behavior

  • activity.Psychological Models: These include the psychodynamic (repressed conflicts), behavioral
  • (learned reactions), and cognitive (illogical thinking patterns) perspectives. Biopsychosocial Model
  • Proposes that disorders arise from the interaction of biological, psychological, and social
  • factors.sociocultural models of disorders
  • Classification: Disorders are primarily classified using the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental
  • Disorders (DSM), which provides standardized criteria for diagnosing various psychological conditions
  • or ICD-11.

questions.question: Explain the concept of observation in psychology, including its advantages and / disadvantages.
questions.solution_html:
• Naturalistic Observation: Involves watching subjects in their everyday environments, offering the
  • advantage of capturing authentic, natural behavior. A major disadvantage is the observer effect, where
  • subjects act differently if they know they are being watched, as well as observer bias
  • Particpant Observation
  • Laboratory Observation: Occurs in a controlled environment, which allows for better use of specialized
  • equipment but may lead to behavior that is less natural than what occurs in the real world
questions.final_answer: equipment but may lead to behavior that is less natural than what occurs in the real world

questions.question: Give a detailed account on the contributions of Sigmund Frued.
questions.solution_html:
• Give a detailed account on the contributions of Sigmund Frued.
  • Answer: Psychoanalysis, the structure of personality (Id, Ego, Superego), the concept of the
  • unconscious, and the psychosexual stages of development. Freud was the founder of the
  • psychodynamic perspective, which posits that many aspects of behavior stem from hidden
  • forces within our personalities and unconscious mind. His key contributions
  • include:Structure of Personality: He divided personality into three parts: the id (the primitive part
  • focused on pleasure), the ego (the rational part that deals with reality), and the superego (the moral center
  • or conscience)Psychosexual Stages: Freud theorized that personality develops through five stages of
  • physical and emotional growth, known as psychosexual stages.Level of Consciousness-The
  • Unconscious: He believed that the unconscious mind stores repressed conflicts and desires that can
  • manifest in outward behavior

questions.question: Explain the concept of observation in psychology, including its advantages and / disadvantages.

  • advantage of capturing authentic, natural behavior. A major disadvantage is the observer effect, where
  • subjects act differently if they know they are being watched, as well as observer bias
  • Particpant Observation

  • equipment but may lead to behavior that is less natural than what occurs in the real world
